anchor.statement: sc-lint's PORT-010 rule must recognize, and not report, a #[cfg(unix)] transport or adapter function or match arm that sits beside a loopback TCP enum variant or function with no #[cfg] guard, which Windows uses instead.
anchor.scope: The item changes when PORT-010 reports or stops reporting a #[cfg(unix)] item in crates/sc-lint-portability.

item.title: Sprint MS4 (#786): PORT-010 transport findings
item.text: Review the remaining PORT-010 findings that atm-core reports on its transport and adapter code, and adjust the PORT-010 rule in crates/sc-lint-portability where those findings are false positives.

relevant.instructions: Is `item.text` about PORT-010's decision to report or not report `#[cfg(unix)]` items? Signals that it is: the item names PORT-010 and says which `#[cfg(unix)]` functions, match arms or other items it reports, stops reporting, treats as covered, or keeps reporting. Signals that it is not: the item names only a different rule (such as PORT-011), a different feature (such as dependency ownership), or no lint rule at all. Judge subject overlap only, not compliance with `anchor.statement`.

criteria.yes: The item names PORT-010 and changes or settles which `#[cfg(unix)]` items it reports.
criteria.no: The item concerns a different rule, a different feature, or no lint rule, and leaves PORT-010's reporting untouched.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions portability work but does not make clear whether PORT-010's reporting of `#[cfg(unix)]` items is involved.

addressed.instructions: Look for one specific change in `item.text`: PORT-010 no longer reports a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter function or match arm when, beside it, there is a loopback TCP enum variant or function that has no `#[cfg]` guard and is what Windows uses. Is that change present in `item.text`? Both parts must be present: (1) PORT-010 stops reporting the `#[cfg(unix)]` item, and (2) the reason is an unguarded loopback TCP sibling. Judge presence only; do not judge conflict.

criteria.yes: Both parts are present: PORT-010 stops reporting (or skips, or treats as covered) the `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter item, and the reason given is a loopback TCP sibling with no `#[cfg]` guard that serves Windows.
criteria.no: At least one part is missing: the item does not mention an unguarded loopback TCP sibling, gives a different sibling such as a `#[cfg(windows)]` function or named pipe, only promises general fixes, or says PORT-010 keeps reporting the item.
criteria.unclear: The item mentions both PORT-010 and a loopback TCP sibling but it is not possible to tell whether PORT-010 stops reporting the `#[cfg(unix)]` item.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` contain a statement that, if carried out, would leave PORT-010 reporting a `#[cfg(unix)]` transport or adapter function or match arm whose loopback TCP sibling has no `#[cfg]` guard and serves Windows? Read the item for its own statement about this case. An item that never mentions this case does not conflict. An item that keeps reporting only cases where the loopback TCP sibling carries a `#[cfg]` guard does not conflict. Judge conflict only.

criteria.yes: The item states that PORT-010 still reports, or will keep reporting, the `#[cfg(unix)]` item in the case where its loopback TCP sibling is unguarded and serves Windows.
criteria.no: The item states no such thing: it stops reporting that case, never mentions it, handles some other shape, or keeps reporting only guarded-sibling cases.
criteria.unclear: The item says something about this case that could be read either way.
